newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps sluggish, Brent CFDs ease back.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps sluggish, Brent CFDs ease back.

text.p: European oil swaps faced a slow day on Thursday with most levels unchanged bar sliding Brent crude CFDs.
"There's a fair degree of lethargy out there," said one dealer. "Its flattering to call it a market," said another.
CFD levels came off further today for the third consecutive day this week in what dealers saw as a rebalancing move after being bid up.

June 2-6 was pegged around -30 cents under July down from 28 under while June 9-13 also slipped to -30 under from -27/28 on Wednesday. June 23-27 was done at August -36 cents, equivalent to -23 cens against July.
High sulphur fuel was steady with only minor tweaking seen during the course of the day. June traded at $83, unchanged against Wednesday.
Low sulphur swaps were also steady, showing a very marginal 25 cent rise according to some dealers. June was pegged around $95, July at $95.50 and August at $96.25.
Naphtha swaps reflected the market's limited volatility with June and July contracts talking flat around $188/$189 and $188.50/$189.50 respectively.
Gasoline barge swaps were unchanged. June contracts talked $204/$205 a tonne with July backwardated by around $5-6 a tonne. A physical barge was sold first half June at $204 fob AR.
